headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: ECC can read/write shared files and use MCP, while unstructured processes documents and can write files, creating unsafe cross-agent handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can use MCP, read/write the filesystem, and run browsers; unstructured reads and writes files in document workflows. If ECC ingests unstructured outputs from a shared workspace, document content can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents exchange files through a shared workspace or document folder
IF ECC parses unstructured output as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated documents
Add a provenance header check before ECC consumes files
Use read-only handoff files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping in the pipeline

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, hooks, and security findings, and can read/write ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc. unstructured processes documents/images/text and writes files. A shared filesystem or copied artifacts could move sensitive session data into document-processing outputs, creating leakage in default multi-tool workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or synced workspace
IF ECC session artifacts are copied into unstructured input documents
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Keep ECC session directories out of document-processing inputs
Restrict unstructured to a dedicated input folder
Review and redact session artifacts before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, install packages, and spawn subprocesses. ECC also modifies git state, while unstructured runs in a docker container. Without explicit locking or separate roots, concurrent writes can collide on shared files or package state, though the container reduces some overlap.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF package installation occurs in a shared environment without locks
mitigations: Assign separate roots/workdirs
Avoid concurrent git operations
Pin package installs to isolated environments
Serialize write-heavy tasks
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can produce security findings, documentation, and code, and unstructured can transform documents into downstream artifacts. If ECC output is fed into unstructured without verification, errors or hallucinated facts can be preserved and propagated into processed documents or subsequent actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so the blast radius can span multiple work products.
conditions: IF ECC-generated text is used as authoritative input for unstructured
IF downstream consumers act on unverified transformed documents
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Require source citations before transformation
Compare outputs against original documents
Mark generated content as untrusted
requires-engineering: add automated verification and provenance tracking

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session summaries, hooks, and security findings with configurable retention and local paths, while unstructured processes documents/images/text and exposes a privacy-policy endpoint. The profiles do not show a direct residency or certification mismatch, but the mixed data classes and retention-sensitive artifacts create a small compliance gap if regulated documents are routed through ECC artifacts.
conditions: IF regulated documents are stored in ECC session artifacts
IF retention settings differ between ECC artifacts and unstructured outputs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in ECC session files
Set explicit retention limits
Document data-class handling for both agents
Review privacy-policy and residency terms before use
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
